record_type_quote: However, note that this GWAS study was conduct only in Caucasian populations [11], and the effects of rs1476679 on other populations are yet unknown. Since variants and their frequencies of ZCWPW1 in various ethnic groups might be different, replication is necessary to confirm the potential effects of ZCWPW1 on other groups. In this study, we firstly conducted the genetic association study on rs1476679 within ZCWPW1 in Han Chinese.

targets.outcome_quote: In consistent with the role of ZCWPW1 (rs1476679) in Caucasians, ZCWPW1 (rs1476679) also acted as a protective factor to the development of AD in Han Chinese.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Independent Han Chinese sample supports the original protective association. Authors explicitly compare the protective direction in their sample with Caucasians. Subgroup and genetic-model variations are not presented as failures to reproduce distinct original findings.

reasoning: Primary association study in a different ethnic sample explicitly tests the rs1476679 finding from the Lambert et al. GWAS discovery report. Although titled meta-analysis, that original is the primary large-scale genetic discovery report, rather than a background review. Ruiz, Xiao and Jiao are discussed as intervening comparisons and pooled in the ancillary meta-analysis; the introduction identifies the original GWAS as the actual finding this new-sample study retests.
